audit_notes: Wrinkle geometry check: lambda = 2*pi*t_s*(E_s/(3*E_b))^(1/3). With the proposed t_s = 3 um, E_s = 50 MPa, E_b = 0.2 MPa: lambda = 2*pi*3e-6*(83.3)^(1/3) = 82 um, above the intended 30-50 um. Adjusted t_s to 1.5 um: lambda = 41 um. Amplitude ~10 um requires a compressive strain of eps ~ eps_c*(1 + (A/t_s)^2*... ) i.e. several percent pre-swelling of the base, feasible. Hydraulic roughness: amplitude 10 um, k_s ~ 5 um, k_s+ = 5/6.3 = 0.8 at 12-16 kn, hydraulically smooth. Settlement model: steady transport of cyprids through a 1 mm near-wall layer (effective diffusivity 1e-6 m^2/s from swimming and port turbulence) with a first-order settlement reaction whose rate is reduced by the texture factor f = 0.5 (attachment-point effect, from lab data up to 0.1 and field ~0.5). Da = delta*k*f/D = 0.005 (design), 0.01 (baseline): reaction-limited, so the gain equals 1 - f = ~50 %. The gain is set by the assumed settlement factor, not by the simulation. Caveats: cyprid response to texture is species-specific (some barnacles prefer grooves of their own scale); diatoms (5-20 um) may prefer the 41 um valleys; the stiff 1.5 um skin can crack under hull strain (critical strain of an oxidised PDMS skin ~1-3 %, hull strain <0.2 %, OK) and wrinkles on soft silicone may flatten under long-term creep. Baseline: smooth conventional foul-release silicone (f = 1). Dimensionless: lambda/antennular disc diameter 41/25 = 1.6, k_s+ = 0.8, Da 0.005. Simulation coefficient: effective settlement velocity 5e-6 m/s (informational).
